what: When a cut-out paper reaches the 90% line of the screen, it bends in a zigzag, moving in two steps per cell (steps(2, end)) over 1.5s and then stops. As in the original (default), it is invisible in place, then pops out sideways 75%·50% (+random ±80·±60px) and up or down −.5·.8x (random −100~100px), tilting ±20° → .7 → −.3x. It is fully visible at 40% and returns to place by 70%. Giving z3·x makes a path flying in from the side at 100%·75%·50%·25%·0. It feels jerky like a paper puppet show, and the bend spots differ each time it opens

options.dir: right (default — from the right) · left · center (rises straight up from below)
options.dur: Duration (s), default 1.5 — 1 for things that open and close like a menu panel
options.start: ScrollTrigger start, default top 90% · if none, right as it sticks
options.z3: Random width (px) beside the third bend — gives life to 70% of cells (no default = Stays in place as in the original)
options.x: Side offset (px) — if given, the 0% stop comes alive and flies in from beside the screen edge (default none = Starts in place, as in the original)
options.z1 · z2: Random sideways width at each bend (px), default 80 · 60

use: <article data-fx="zigzag-step-in" data-fx-zigzag-step-in="dir: left">…</article>  · Fly in from the side: data-fx-zigzag-step-in="dir: left; z3: 40; x: 0"
note: The original CSS does not define --zig3 or --offset-x, so the transform in those cells (0% and 70%, 40% for center) is invalid at compute time, and Chrome draws those cells in place (matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)) (confirmed by a keyframes test on 2026-11-03). The part default follows that actual motion. To get ”fly in from the side”, use data-fx-zigzag-step-in="z3: 40; x: 0"

from.where: shared.css [data-direction] zigzag-left/right/center-random (original .js-zigzag — program cards · shadow images · splash leaves · paper menu. 1.5s steps(2,end), once at the 90% screen line)
from.options: dir: left | right | center (a set of three cards goes in the order left·center·right)
